_meta.note: SYNTHETIC SEED DATA. These policy snippets are representative procurement-policy wordings written for the ProcureAI demo so the audit agent can cite a policy section behind its verdict. They are NOT any real company's policy.

policies.text: Invoices from the same vendor against the same purchase order whose total amounts agree within 2% and whose invoice dates fall within 45 days of each other shall be treated as suspected duplicate billings. The later invoice must be held for manual review; it must not be paid automatically.
policies.title: Duplicate Invoice Detection

policies.text: Splitting a single procurement into multiple invoices to stay below the $10,000 management approval threshold is prohibited. An invoice total within $500 below the $10,000 threshold, especially from a vendor with a related invoice on the same purchase order, shall be flagged as possible split billing for human review.
policies.title: Split Billing Below Approval Threshold

policies.text: Unit prices billed on an invoice must not exceed the purchase order contracted rate by more than 10%. Any line item priced more than 10% above its contracted rate requires written vendor justification before approval.
policies.title: Contracted Price Variance

policies.text: Payments may only be issued to vendors present in the approved vendor master file. A vendor missing from the master file, or whose tax ID is unverified, must be treated as a suspected ghost vendor and the invoice rejected pending vendor onboarding verification.
policies.title: Approved Vendor Requirement

policies.text: Vendors with two or fewer prior invoices on record, or with a risk rating at or above 0.70, are subject to enhanced review. High risk rating combined with thin invoice history is a fraud indicator and must be flagged even when the arithmetic is correct.
policies.title: Thin-History Vendor Review

policies.text: Line item totals must sum exactly to the invoice subtotal, and subtotal plus tax must equal the invoiced total. Tax is assessed at the standard 8% rate on the subtotal. Any arithmetic discrepancy, however small, is grounds for rejection of the invoice as billed in error or with intent to overcharge.
policies.title: Arithmetic Accuracy and Tax

policies.text: The total amount billed on an invoice must not exceed the amount limit of its governing purchase order. Invoices billed above the purchase order limit shall be rejected unless a formal change order increasing the limit is on record.
policies.title: Purchase Order Threshold Limit

policies.text: Every audit verdict must cite the evidence that produced it: arithmetic verification results with exact figures, purchase order limit comparison, vendor standing, duplicate search outcome, and the anomaly score. A verdict that cannot cite its evidence is not a valid audit outcome.
policies.title: Evidence-Backed Verdicts
